Chandra.name: Chandra Deva
Chandra.note: Chandra Deva (also Soma), the radiant deva of the moon and of the soma nectar; progenitor and eponym of the Chandravamsha, the lunar dynasty from which both the Kurus and the Yadavas descend.

Budha.name: Budha Deva
Budha.note: Budha Deva, the deva of the planet Mercury and son of Chandra; husband of Ila.

Pururavas.note: Son of Budha and Ila; first emperor of the lunar line, famed for his love of the apsara Urvashi. She agreed to live with him on three conditions — never to be seen naked by him, and her two pet rams never harmed — and the Gandharvas broke the compact for her by stealing the rams in the dark, so that he leapt up unclothed by lightning-flash to chase them off; she vanished at once, and he wandered mad with grief until the Gandharvas, moved by it, let them meet again, an evening at a time, and Ayus was born of those nights.

Nahusha.note: Son of Ayus; so mighty he briefly took Indra's throne, then fell for his pride and became a serpent. Made regent-Indra while the real Indra hid from the sin of killing the brahmin Vritra; grew so arrogant on the throne he had the seven sages carry his palanquin, and kicked the slow sage Agastya in his impatience, who cursed him to fall to earth as a python. Lived on as a giant serpent, caught and questioned Bhima in its coils during the exile, and was freed of the curse when Yudhishthira answered its riddles.

Yayati.note: Son of Nahusha; a great emperor cursed with old age, which his youngest son Puru bore for him. His five sons founded five peoples. Cursed by his father-in-law Shukracharya for taking a second wife, Sharmishtha, behind his first wife Devayani's back; exchanged the curse's old age for a thousand years of his son Puru's youth, exhausted every pleasure without satisfaction, and returned it, naming Puru his heir over his elder sons for the sacrifice. Fell from heaven later for pride, and was carried back up on the merit his grandsons through Madhavi gave him.

Yadu.note: Eldest son of Yayati and Devayani; progenitor of the Yadavas (the Yadu line), into which Krishna is born.

Turvasu.note: Son of Yayati and Devayani; ancestor of the Yavana peoples.

Druhyu.note: Son of Yayati and Sharmishtha; ancestor of the Bhoja peoples.

Anu.note: Son of Yayati and Sharmishtha; ancestor of the Mleccha peoples.

Puru.note: Youngest son of Yayati and Sharmishtha; he gave his own youth to his aged father and so inherited the throne, founding the Paurava (Kuru) line.

Dushyanta.note: A Paurava emperor descended from Puru through several generations; husband of Shakuntala and father of Bharata.

Bharata.note: The great emperor son of Dushyanta and Shakuntala, after whom the land Bharatavarsha and the Bharata clan are named. Tested as a boy at Kanva's ashram playing fearlessly with lion cubs, counting their teeth; recognised by Dushyanta only after the king's ring, lost and found in a fish, restored his memory of Shakuntala; passed over his own sons for the throne and adopted the sage Bharadvaja's son Vitatha instead, since none of his own were found worthy.

people.Hastin: Son of Brihatkshatra; he built Hastinapura, which carries his name. SB 9.21.21

Kuru.note: King some generations after Hastin; eponymous ancestor of the Kurus and of the field of Kurukshetra. Ploughed the field himself and sowed it with grains of penance rather than corn, at Indra's asking, to make it forever a ground where any who died fighting or in austerity there would reach heaven — the reason the war his own descendants fought is staged exactly there.

Kroshtu.note: Son of Yadu; the Yadava kings descend from him.

Vrijinivat.note: A Yadava king, son of Kroshtu.

Swahi.note: A Yadava king of the early Yadu line.

Rushadru.note: A Yadava king of the early Yadu line.

Madhu.note: A Yadava king; progenitor of the Madhava branch, whence Krishna's epithet Madhava. Several generations separate him from Vrishni.

people.Vrishni: Son of Satvata, and the Vrishni for whom the clan of Krishna is named. SB 9.24.6-12

Amavasu.note: Son of Pururavas; founder of the Kanyakubja (Kaushika) branch of the lunar line.

Gadhi.note: King of the Kaushikas; father of Vishvamitra and of Satyavati, who married the sage Richika and bore Jamadagni. Vishvamitra's own royal birth, before his penance won him brahmin status, runs through Gadhi.

Ajamidha.note: Son of Hastin; founder of the Ajamidha branch of the Puru line, from whom Panchala and Kuru both descend. SB 9.21.

Riksha.note: Son of Ajamidha; ancestor of the Kuru line.

JanamejayaP.name: Janamejaya
JanamejayaP.note: Son of Puru. Not Parikshit's son. SB 9.20.1

people.Raudrashva: Ten sons by the apsara Ghritachi: Riteyu, Kaksheyu, Sthandileyu, Kriteyuka, Jaleyu, Sannateyu, Dharmeyu, Satyeyu, Vrateyu and Vaneyu. SB 9.20.3-4
people.Rantinava: Three sons: Sumati, Dhruva and Apratiratha, whose son Kanva raised Shakuntala. SB 9.20.6

Vitatha.name: Vitatha (Bharadvaja)
Vitatha.note: Bharata's sacrifices gave him no worthy heir, and Bharadvaja, the son Brihaspati begot on Mamata, was given to him instead: given away he is Vitatha, the one who was otherwise. The same sage appears in this tree in his own right, in the Angirasa line, as the father of Drona. SB 9.20.37-38

people.Manyu: Five sons: Brihatkshatra, Jaya, Mahavirya, Nara and Garga. SB 9.21.19
people.Sankriti: Son of Nara; father of Guru and of Rantideva. SB 9.21.1
people.Rantideva: He gave away his own food until he and his household fasted. After forty-eight days without even water, food came, and with it a brahmin guest, then a shudra, then a stranger, then a thirsty man for the last of the water: he gave each of them everything, and asked for nothing but that all beings be free of suffering. SB 9.21.2-18
people.Garga: Son of Manyu; his line, kshatriya by birth, became brahmins. SB 9.21.19, 9.21.31
people.Kshatravriddha: Son of Ayus, from whom the kings of Kashi descend. SB 9.17.1
people.Raji: Son of Ayus. Indra gave him the kingdom of heaven for his help against the demons; his five hundred sons would not give it back, and Brihaspati's rites unmade their intelligence until Indra took it. SB 9.17.1, 9.17.10-17
people.Rabha: Son of Ayus. His line: Rabhasa, Gambhira, Akriya, Brahmavit. SB 9.17.1, 9.17.11

AnenaS.name: Anena
AnenaS.note: Son of Ayus. His line: Shuddha, Shuchi, Chitrakrit, Shantaraja. Not Anena of the solar line. SB 9.17.1, 9.17.11

SahasrajitY.name: Sahasrajit
SahasrajitY.note: Eldest of Yadu's four sons; the Haihayas descend from him. SB 9.23.20-21

NalaY.name: Nala
NalaY.note: Third son of Yadu. Not Nala of Nishadha, nor Nala the vanara. SB 9.23.20

ChitrarathaY.name: Chitraratha
ChitrarathaY.note: Son of Rushadru in the Kroshtu line. Not Chitraratha the Gandharva. SB 9.23.31

people.Prithushrava: Foremost among Shashabindu's sons, with Prithukirti. SB 9.23.33
people.Ushana: Performer of a hundred horse sacrifices. SB 9.23.33
people.Rucaka: Five sons: Purujit, Rukma, Rukmeshu, Prithu and Jyamagha. SB 9.23.34
people.Jyamagha: Sonless, and too afraid of his barren queen Shaibya to take another wife. He brought a captive girl home on his chariot, and when Shaibya demanded to know who sat in her seat he said, your daughter-in-law. The devas made the words true: Shaibya bore Vidarbha, and Vidarbha grew up and married the girl. SB 9.23.34-38
people.Vidarbha: Born to Jyamagha and Shaibya by the mercy of the devas; three sons, Kusha, Kratha and Romapada. The Vidarbha kingdom keeps his name. SB 9.23.38, 9.24.1
people.Kratha: Son of Vidarbha; the Vrishni line runs through him. SB 9.24.1, 9.24.3

VrishniI.name: Vrishni
VrishniI.note: Son of Kunti of the Kratha line, generations above the Vrishni for whom the clan is named. SB 9.24.3

people.Dasharha: The Dasharhas take their name from him. SB 9.24.3

ShakuniY.name: Shakuni
ShakuniY.note: Son of Dasharatha of the Yadava line. Not Shakuni of Gandhara. SB 9.24.5

Shaibya.note: Queen of Jyamagha, barren and jealous, whose sharp question became a blessing: she bore Vidarbha, and the captive girl she had objected to became her daughter-in-law. SB 9.23.35-38

AnuY.name: Anu
AnuY.note: Son of Kuruvasha. Not Anu the son of Yayati. SB 9.24.5

people.Satvata: Seven sons: Bhajamana, Bhaji, Divya, Vrishni, Devavridha, Andhaka and Mahabhoja, and the branches of the whole Yadava house run from them. SB 9.24.6-8
people.Shrutayu: Son of Pururavas and Urvashi; his son was Vasuman. SB 9.15.1-2
people.Satyayu: Son of Pururavas and Urvashi; his son was Shrutanjaya. SB 9.15.1-2
people.Raya: Son of Pururavas and Urvashi; his son was Eka. SB 9.15.1-2

JayaP.name: Jaya
JayaP.note: Son of Pururavas and Urvashi; his son was Amita. SB 9.15.1-2

VijayaP.name: Vijaya
VijayaP.note: Son of Pururavas and Urvashi. SB 9.15.1-2

Madhavi.note: Daughter of Yayati, given not in marriage but in loan: her blessing was that she recovered her maidenhood after each birth and that her sons would be kings. Galava lent her to three kings for two hundred white horses each and to Vishvamitra for the last two hundred, and she bore Vasumanas, Pratardana, Shibi and Ashtaka. Offered a svayamvara afterwards she chose the forest instead and lived as a deer lives. When Yayati fell out of heaven for pride, these four grandsons gave him the merit of their sacrifices and raised him back. MBh 5.113-121
